```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(cytoJointR)
# Optional packages: chunks that need them run only when they are installed.
has_pkg <- function(p) nzchar(system.file(package = p)) && requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)
has_compass <- has_pkg("COMPASS")
has_polyics <- has_pkg("polyICSFlow")
```

This vignette goes from one row per event to gated patterns, COMPASS and
polyICSFlow scores, and the fluorescence-aware scores of cytoJointR. It uses
simulated cells, so the true gate is known (fluorescence 0).
Optional packages (COMPASS: `r if (has_compass) "installed" else "not installed, its chunk is shown but not run"`;
polyICSFlow: `r if (has_polyics) "installed" else "not installed, its chunk is shown but not run"`)
are checked at run time.

## Cells and samples

`cells` has one row per event: `sample_id` and one fluorescence column per
marker. Events must already be inside the parent population (for example live
CD4 T cells). `samples` has one row per sample with `donor_id`, `visit` (a factor
with explicit levels), `parent_population` and `condition`.

```{r data}
sim <- cj_simulate_cells(donors = 10, cells_per_sample = 1500, seed = 1)
cells <- sim$cells
markers <- c("IFNG", "TNF", "IL2")
samples <- unique(cells[c("sample_id", "donor_id", "condition")])
samples$visit <- factor("v1")
samples$parent_population <- "CD4"
head(cells[c("sample_id", markers)], 3)
table(samples$condition)
```

The simulator calls the unstimulated sample `"unstim"`. The package wants
`"control"` internally, so every function takes `control = "unstim"` and
recodes it.

## Gate

`cj_gate()` finds one threshold per marker on all control events pooled over
donors. The transform must be stated: `"none"` means these cells are already on
the analysis scale. For raw fluorescence use `transform = "asinh"` with a
`cofactor`, or pass a function.

```{r gate}
gate <- cj_gate(cells, markers, samples, transform = "none", control = "unstim")
gate
```

The default `"tail"` method runs in base R. It takes the main peak of the
pooled control density as the negative population and puts the cut 3.09 spreads
above it. `method = "quantile"` takes a control quantile. `method = "mindensity"`
calls `openCyto::gate_mindensity()` when openCyto is installed (otherwise it
warns and uses the quantile). `thresholds = c(IFNG = 0.3, ...)` sets them by hand.
Always look at the gate.

```{r gate-plot}
cj_plot_gate(gate)
```

Here the true gate is 0. The tail gate misclassifies
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mean(unlist(lapply(markers, function(m) (cells[[m]] > gate$thresholds[[m]]) != (cells[[m]] > 0)))))`
of cells against it.

## Cells to `cj_data`

`cj_from_cells()` applies the gate, tabulates exact patterns per sample and
returns the same `cj_data` the count workflow uses, so `cj_describe()`,
`cj_fit()` and `cj_scores()` work on it. It also keeps the per-pattern sums of
`X - t` and `(X - t)^2` that the fluorescence scores need.

```{r data-object}
x <- cj_from_cells(cells, samples = samples, gate = gate)
x
dim(x$intensity$sx)  # sample x pattern x marker
```

## Fluorescence-aware scores

`cj_fluorescence_scores()` returns one row per donor, stimulation, visit and
marker. All scores are descriptive: plug-in estimates from the events, in
transformed fluorescence units per parent cell. Donors without a control are
listed and omitted.

```{r fluor}
fs <- cj_fluorescence_scores(x, n_boot = 100, seed = 1)
head(fs[c("donor_id", "marker", "nicr", "nicr_lo", "nicr_hi", "poly_nicr", "iw_pfs")], 6)
```

* `nicr`: net integrated cytokine response of the marker, stimulated minus
  control burden. Markers are never summed.
* `poly_nicr`: the same over patterns with two or more positive markers.
* `nicr_freq`, `nicr_int`, `nicr_unmatched`: an exact split of `nicr` into a
  change in how many cells are in each pattern and a change in how bright they
  are. They add up to `nicr`:

```{r decomp}
with(fs, max(abs(nicr - nicr_freq - nicr_int - nicr_unmatched)))
```

* `fis`: intensity shift under fixed reference weights, `NA` with a reason where
  a reference pattern has no cells. Controls hold few polyfunctional cells, so
  use `reference = "single"` to ask for the shift among cells positive for that
  marker alone.
* `iw_fs`, `iw_pfs` (experimental): COMPASS's FS and PFS weights applied to the
  net burden of each marker in each subset instead of a response probability.

```{r fis}
fs1 <- cj_fluorescence_scores(x, reference = "single")
table(fis_available = !is.na(fs1$fis))
```

The bootstrap resamples events within each sample. Its intervals cover cell
sampling only. Donors are the replicates, so compare groups across donors.

```{r nicr-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
d <- fs[fs$marker == "IFNG", ]
d$donor_id <- factor(d$donor_id, levels = d$donor_id[order(d$nicr)])
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(.data$nicr, .data$donor_id)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(xmin = .data$nicr_lo, xmax = .data$nicr_hi)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "NICR of IFNG (transformed units per parent cell), 95% cell bootstrap",
                y = NULL)
```

## COMPASS and polyICSFlow

`cj_run_compass()` wraps `cj_compass()` and returns a tidy FS, PFS and response
table per donor. The full `cj_compass` object is in `attr(, "compass")`.

```{r compass, eval = has_compass}
cp <- cj_run_compass(x, iterations = 200, replications = 2, seed = 1)
head(cp[c("donor_id", "compass_FS", "compass_PFS")], 4)
```

A stimulated sample without a control is dropped by default. Set
`missing_control = "donor"` to borrow the same donor's control from the nearest
other visit, or `"population"` to compare the sample with the other donors'
controls (COMPASS integrates out each donor's control proportions, so a zero
control row contributes nothing). The `control_source` column says which rows
were not paired. A borrowed control assumes the background does not change
between visits, and the population control assumes this donor's background is
like the others'; see `docs/adr/0003-compass-missing-control.md` for the
simulation behind these cautions.

```{r compass-missing, eval = FALSE}
cj_run_compass(x, missing_control = "donor", iterations = 200, replications = 2)
```

`cj_run_polyicsflow()` runs polyICSFlow's marker-combination and
background-subtraction functions on the same counts. polyICSFlow clips each
pattern at zero, so `polyics_net_any` is not the signed net percent of
`cj_describe()`.

```{r polyics, eval = has_polyics}
pf <- cj_run_polyicsflow(x)
head(pf$net)
```

## Everything at once

`cj_quickstart()` chains gate, data, description, fluorescence scores and, when
installed, COMPASS and polyICSFlow. Add `fit = TRUE` (and `epsilon`) to fit the
count model and get the cytoJointR scores; that needs CmdStan.

```{r quickstart}
qs <- cj_quickstart(cells, markers, samples, transform = "none", control = "unstim",
                    run = character())
names(qs)
```
